author: DVY
text_post: Careful w/massive doses of citrus aka acid. Esp biting into limes/lemons/oranges. The acid erodes your enamel and causes erosion and notching on the gingival portion of your teeth.  The stephan curve, summarizes, what happens in your mouth with acid consumption. Any environment w/a pH below 5.5 causes enamel and dentin resorption. Saliva/water helps buffer the pH and minimize damage. This occurs within the next 30 minutes.  Your saliva level slows/minimizes after age 40. This coupled w/most-medications( 80% cause xerostomia, or dry mouth) means acid-buffering takes up to 3-4 times as long. So, recommend topical fluoride supplements or flushing your mouth w/water after heavy acid consumption. Also eat regular meals and don't snack constantly as it is not just the quantity of food/drink but the frequency. Babies who have sippy-cups that they can drink all day have horrible teeth....
